description: A loop of moving paper and four brushes: four control voltages are drawn onto it by mouse or from the patch, and four read heads play them back

params.text: Sets how fast the paper moves, -4 to 4 times; negative runs it backwards
Sets how much paper goes round; it is a length in cells rather than a duration, so running faster shortens the loop instead of squashing what is drawn on it
Smooths what the read heads pick up, without changing what is drawn
Sets how much ink a pass lays down
Sets how much ink a pass lifts; balanced against the ink knob it sets whether repeated passes build up or wash out
Returns the paper to its start on each press
Points the mouse at that lane, so drawing on the paper writes to it
Points the mouse at erasing rather than at a lane
Fans the four read heads apart along the paper, ±100 per cent

inputs.text: Draws that lane from a voltage instead of the mouse
While this is high the draw CV inputs record onto the paper and while it is low they do not; unpatched, they always record, despite the tooltip calling this jack retired
Each rise advances the paper one cell
Marks the bar, for the clocks-per-bar setting on the menu
Changes the paper speed, added to the speed knob
Changes the smoothing, added to the slew knob
Changes how much ink a pass lays down, added to the ink knob
A high gate runs the paper, taking the run button's place
A high gate runs the paper backwards, taking the reverse button's place
A rise returns the paper to its start
Moves that lane's own read head along the paper, added to the spread
Sets how thick that lane's stroke is as it is drawn, which is also that lane's velocity
Changes how far the read heads are fanned apart, added to the spread knob
Changes how much ink a pass lifts, added to the leak knob

outputs.text: The line under that lane's read head
How much ink is on the paper under that lane's read head

notes: nothing comes out until something has been drawn: the paper starts blank and the outputs rest until a brush or a draw CV has laid a line down
the paper moves whether or not anything is being drawn, so where the mouse is sets what a stroke does: left of the playhead it edits, right of it it composes ahead, on it it performs
a brush cannot write while the paper is running backwards, because a stroke laid over paper moving the other way would retrace and eat itself
each lane also reports where its line turns around: the slope is classed as rising, falling or flat, and events fire on the changes, so a scribble makes notes at its turning points
menu: Lane 1 — a submenu of that lane's own settings
Range: Bipolar +/-5V, Unipolar 0-10V — sets the voltage span that lane's value output covers
Read: Smooth, Stepped (sharp edges) — chooses whether that lane's read is interpolated or held in steps
Quantize — snaps that lane's value output to a grid
Clear lane — wipes what is drawn on that lane
Copy to lane 2 — copies that lane's drawing onto another, which with the heads fanned apart gives several reads of one gesture
Stroke weight: Hairline, Fine, Normal, Bold, Heavy — sets how far the ink is allowed to swing the drawn line's width
Clocks per bar: 1, 2, 4, 8, 12, 16, 24, 32 — says how many clock pulses make a bar
Clear all paper — wipes every lane
